role: Publishes the names a cluster is reached at — members, capabilities and game servers — and is the only member holding a credential for the zone.

fields.label: Listen address
fields.description: The address this anchor listens on. It sits behind the machine's web server, which holds the certificate and answers the public name.

fields.label: Cluster member id
fields.description: The name other members of the cluster know this anchor by. A machine can run more than one member — a node and an anchor are two members with two names — so this is not the machine's name. Blank derives one from it.

fields.label: Public address
fields.description: The address other members of the cluster reach this anchor at. Set it when this machine sits behind a reverse proxy and cannot see its own public address; otherwise leave it blank and the addresses are learned when a member joins.

fields.label: This machine's public host
fields.description: Where this machine is reached from the internet — normally the dynamic-DNS name its network already keeps pointed at a changing home address, such as example.ddns.net. The capability's name points here, so an address change needs nothing from this anchor. A fixed public address works too. Blank leaves the capability's name unpublished.

fields.label: Zone
fields.description: The domain this cluster publishes names in, such as example.com. One domain is all a cluster needs: members, capabilities and game servers are named underneath it.

fields.label: Members are named under
fields.description: The part of the domain members are named under. With nodes, a member is reached at something like jessie.nodes.example.com.

fields.label: Capabilities are named under
fields.description: The part of the domain capabilities are named under. With anchors, the cluster's sign-in is reached at something like auth.anchors.example.com.

fields.label: Game servers are named under
fields.description: The part of the domain game servers are named under. With play, a server is played at something like minecraft.play.example.com.

fields.label: Member names
fields.description: The names members are given when they join, one of which is drawn at random for each. Nothing on a machine has to be configured with what that machine is called.

fields.label: Pinned member names
fields.description: Members that keep a name they already answer to, written as member=name. A machine people already reach at a name goes on being reached there when it joins.

fields.label: Provider
fields.description: The DNS provider this cluster's zone is hosted with.

fields.label: Zone id
fields.description: The provider's identifier for the zone. Its dashboard shows it beside the domain.

fields.label: API token
fields.description: The API token this anchor changes the zone with. It is held by this member alone, which is why every other member asks this one for a name instead of carrying a credential of its own.

fields.label: Record lifetime
fields.description: How long other computers remember an answer before asking again. Short, because a member changing address or a capability moving to another member takes effect only once the old answer has expired everywhere.

fields.label: Zone check interval
fields.description: How often this anchor checks that the zone still says what the cluster asked it to say. It is what heals a record edited by hand and a write that failed halfway.

fields.label: Certificate issuer
fields.description: The certificate issuer this anchor orders from. Let's Encrypt's production directory issues certificates browsers trust; its staging directory issues ones they do not, for trying the whole path without spending the issuer's limits.

fields.label: Issuer contact
fields.description: An email address the issuer may write to about this cluster's certificates. Blank registers the account with no contact.

fields.label: Issuer account key
fields.description: The key this anchor's account with the issuer is registered under. Generated on first use and never copied: a member that takes this capability over registers its own.

fields.label: Allowed browser origins
fields.description: The browser origins allowed to read this anchor's page, comma-separated — normally the Control Panel's address. The panel is served from a different origin, so without an entry for it the browser refuses the answer before the page can read it.

fields.label: Name registry
fields.description: The file this anchor records every claimed name in. It can be rebuilt from the zone itself, because each record says which cluster name it is.

fields.label: Cluster store
fields.description: The file this member keeps its cluster membership in — who else is in the cluster, and the messages owed to them.

fields.label: Account copy
fields.description: This anchor's own copy of the cluster's accounts, filled by the member that holds them. It is what decides who may read this page, read afresh on every request.

fields.label: Ended sessions
fields.description: The sessions somebody signed out of elsewhere in the cluster, kept so this anchor refuses them too until they would have expired.

fields.label: Config descriptor
fields.description: The file describing what this anchor can be configured with, written by its own build and installed by its deploy. It is read to render this page; absent, there is no page.

fields.label: Log level
fields.description: Minimum severity this anchor logs.
